reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) confirms the context of ATF cladding development and mentions Cr coatings and Al-containing materials, but neither passage provides specific prior evidence that an Al interlayer forms an Al2O3 diffusion barrier, limits Cr–Zr interdiffusion, or preserves coating integrity under the stated dual conditions. The key mechanistic and performance premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Elemental Cr coatings on Zr-alloy cladding suffer from Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures, causing premature failure.
An Al interlayer can form a dense, adherent Al2O3 barrier at the Cr–Zr interface at elevated temperatures.
An Al2O3 barrier effectively limits Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The Al interlayer preserves coating adherence and oxidation resistance under both normal PWR and high-temperature steam conditions.
